blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en:
Thinking-enabled vision-language models (VLMs) report ever-higher accuracy on spatial benchmarks, yet final-answer scores cannot reveal whether a correct prediction reflects faithful spatial reasoning or a linguistic shortcut.
We introduce SpatialChain , a dataset of 28,350 training and 899 test examples pairing spatially-oriented GQA questions with scene-graph-grounded reasoning chains — retained only when the generated answer matches the symbolic ground truth — and a two-axis evaluation combining objective chain-overlap metrics with a scene-graph-aware LLM judge that scores faithfulness and completeness independently of the final answer.
Applied to nine thinking-enabled VLMs, the protocol surfaces three findings invisible to standard accuracy: (i) four of nine models achieve ≥ 79 % \geq\!79\% VQA accuracy while exhibiting shortcut rates above 39 % 39\% — correct answers whose reasoning the judge marks as unfaithful; (ii) chain quality significantly predicts answer correctness for seven of nine models, but the two exceptions (Claude Sonnet 4.6, InternVL3.5-8B) reveal qualitatively distinct failure modes — terse output vs. verbose-decorative reasoning — that benchmark accuracy alone conflates; (iii) SFT on SpatialChain improves Qwen3-VL-8B by + 6.2 +6.2 pp in-domain and reduces its shortcut rate to 22 % 22\% , while a possible stylistic specialization effect on external benchmarks motivates replay-augmented training as mitigation.
The faithfulness judge is validated against 198 human-annotated items, where judge–human agreement matches human–human agreement, and against a second judge from a different provider, which preserves the model ranking ( ρ = 0.88 \rho=0.88 ).
Data, generation scripts, and evaluation code are released at github.com/spatialchain/SpatialChainBenchmark .

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en: Vision-language models (VLMs) have achieved remarkable performance on visual question answering (VQA) and spatial understanding benchmarks [ 40 , 23 ] . More recently, several model families have been augmented with explicit multimodal reasoning, including Qwen3-VL [ 3 ] , InternVL3 [ 37 ] , GLM-4.1-9B [ 9 ] , Claude 4.6 [ 2 ] , and GPT-5.4 [ 26 ] . These thinking-enabled models drive substantial gains on challenging benchmarks [ 41 , 36 , 7 ] , yet high accuracy alone does not establish that a model is reasoning rather than exploiting statistical language priors. A model that has memorized common object co-occurrences (e.g., cup on table , person on chair ) may answer spatial queries correctly without performing any actual spatial inference. Standard benchmarks provide no mechanism to distinguish these two regimes: only the final answer is evaluated, leaving the underlying reasoning process entirely unaudited [ 8 , 1 , 25 , 6 ] .
blocks.zh: 视觉语言模型(VLMs)在视觉问答(VQA)和空间理解基准[40,23]上取得了显著的性能. 最近,几个模范家庭通过明确的多模式推理得到扩充,包括:Qune3-VL[3]、InternVL3[37]、GLM-4.1-9B。 [9],克洛德 4.6 [2],和GPT-5.4 [26]. 这些启发思考的模式推动在具有挑战性的基准[41、36、7]方面取得实质性进展,然而,仅靠高准确性并不能确定一个模式是推理而不是利用统计语言的前传。 记忆了常见物体并发的模型(如桌上的杯子,椅子上的人)可以正确回答空间询问而无需进行任何实际的空间推论. 标准基准没有为区分这两种制度提供机制:只有最后答案才得到评价,使基本推理过程完全没有经过审计[8、1、25、6]。

blocks.en:
To address this, we present SpatialChain , which attaches an explicit, graph-grounded reasoning chain to each spatially-oriented question drawn from GQA [ 11 ] . Every chain is synthesized from GQA’s structured scene graphs via Claude Haiku 4.5 with extended thinking, retained only when the generated answer matches the ground-truth answer, and stored in a format compatible with thinking-mode VLMs.
Because each reasoning step derives from a verifiable symbolic annotation, SpatialChain enables a new evaluation regime: beyond did the model answer correctly , we can ask did its reasoning trace engage with the correct spatial relations — and detect shortcut behavior even when the final answer is right.

为了解决这一问题,我们介绍SpaceChain ,它从GQA[11]中抽取的每个面向空间的问题都附有一个明确、以图表为基础的推理链。 每个链由GQA结构化的场景图通过Claude Haiku 4.5来合成,具有延伸的思维,只有在生成的答案与地上真实的答案相匹配时才保留,并以与思维-模式VLM相兼容的格式被保存.
因为每个推理步骤都来自可核查的符号注释, SpaceChain 使新的评价制度得以实现:除了模型答案正确外,我们可以问其推理追踪是否与正确的空间关系有关——即使最后答案正确,也可以检测捷径行为.

blocks.en: 2 Related Work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en: Thinking-enabled VLMs have driven substantial gains on general VQA suites [ 40 , 41 ] and on dedicated spatial benchmarks such as EmbSpatial-Bench [ 7 ] , ERQA [ 32 ] , VSR [ 20 ] , and VSI-Bench [ 39 ] ; SpatialRGPT [ 5 ] further improves spatial perception by grounding VLMs in 3D scene graphs, while recent probes expose persistent failures on geometric consistency and subtle spatial comparisons [ 14 , 15 ] . All of these benchmarks share the same structural limitation: they score only the final answer, providing no mechanism to determine whether a correct prediction reflects genuine spatial inference or a linguistic shortcut [ 8 , 1 ] . GQA [ 11 ] exposes relational structure through scene graphs that could in principle support process-level evaluation, but its standard protocol is equally answer-only.
blocks.zh: 思维驱动 VLM在普通VQA套件[40,41]和专用空间基准(如EmbSpatial-Bench [7]、ERQA [32]、VSR [20]和VSI-Bench [39])上取得了巨大进展;空间RGPT [5] 通过将VLMs放入3D场景图来进一步改善空间感知,而最近的探测则暴露出几何一致性和微妙空间比较的持续失败[14,15]. 所有这些基准都具有相同的结构限制:它们只得分最后的答案,没有提供机制来确定正确的预测是反映真实的空间推论还是语言快捷[8, 1]. GQA [11] 通过场景图曝光关系结构,原则上可以支持进程级评价,但其标准协议同样只回答.

blocks.en: Inspired by chain-of-thought prompting [ 38 ] , several efforts expose the reasoning process alongside the final answer. ScienceQA [ 24 ] and VCR [ 42 ] provide human rationales in specialised domains, with free-form text that lacks structured grounding to image content. A more targeted line associates reasoning steps with image regions — Visual-CoT [ 30 ] , CogCoM [ 27 ] , DualFocus [ 4 ] , Chain-of-Spot [ 22 ] , and, at scale, VisReason [ 18 ] — and EmbodiedVSR [ 45 ] uses dynamic scene graphs to guide chain-of-thought on spatial tasks. Closer to our evaluation goal, SpatialEval [ 35 ] scores final answers on spatial tasks without auditing the trace, and MME-CoT [ 12 ] evaluates reasoning quality against free-form or human-written rationales without structured grounding to image content. These resources advance visual grounding — where to look — but none provides a verifiable reference for the relational content of a chain: a model that crops the correct region but reasons about the wrong spatial relation remains indistinguishable from one that genuinely understands the scene. SpatialChain fills this gap by deriving every reasoning step from GQA’s structured scene graphs and retaining chains only when consistent with the symbolic ground truth, enabling an evaluation that asks not only did the model look at the right region but did it reason about the correct spatial relations .
blocks.zh: 受思维链的启发[38],一些努力暴露了推理过程与最后答案。 ScienceQA[24]和VCR[42]在专门领域提供了人的理由,其中自由格式的文字缺乏结构化地打入图像内容的基础. 更有针对性的线条将推理步骤与图像区域联系起来——视觉-CoT[30],CogCoM[27], DualFocus [4],"地铁链"[22],并按规模,维斯瑞生[18]——和"EmformiveVSR"[45]使用动态场景图来指导空间任务的思维链. 更接近于我们的评价目标,SpaceEval [35] 在空间任务上评分最终答案,而不审核跟踪,而MME-CoT [12] 对照自由形式或人文理由评价推理质量,而不对图像内容进行结构化地基. 这些资源推进了视地定位——在哪里看——但没有任何资源为链条的关系内容提供可核查的参考:这种模型收割了正确的区域,但错误的空间关系的理由与真正了解现场的模型仍然无法区分。 空间 链条通过从GQA结构化的场景图中得出每一个推理步骤来填补这一空白, 并且只有在符合象征性的地面真实性时才保留链条,

blocks.en:

budget 3,000 tokens, max output 4,096 tokens) via the Anthropic

The generated chain must therefore use natural visual language,
producing traces indistinguishable from those a human annotator would
write when looking at the image.

blocks.en: 3.4 Dataset Statistics
blocks.zh: 3.4 数据集统计

blocks.en:
SpatialChain comprises 28,350 training and 899 test question–reasoning–answer triplets drawn from 19,263 and 719 unique images respectively (Table 1 ). The relation distribution is dominated by projective relations: left_of / right_of account for 62.7 % of training questions under our first-occurrence labelling scheme, where each question is tagged according to the first spatial relation appearing in its string. Thus, these statistics indicate the entry point of the spatial chain rather than its complete relational content, since many questions combine multiple relations, especially in the test split.
In the test split this dominance follows from the complexity-biased selection (§ 3.2 ) — GQA’s longest chains are built from projective relations — so per-relation cells with n < 20 n<20 are non-inferential.
Training chains have a mean length of 115 words (median 112), and test chains are slightly longer (mean 145 words), reflecting the complexity-biased test selection. Full relation and chain-length breakdowns are in Appendix D .

blocks.en: 4 Evaluation Framework
blocks.zh: 4 评价框架

blocks.en: We evaluate models along two complementary axes: downstream accuracy on the VQA task, and reasoning quality assessed through objective corpus metrics and an LLM-based judge. The former measures whether the model produces the correct answer; the latter examines whether it does so for the right reasons.
blocks.zh: 我们沿着两个互补轴对模型进行评估:对VQA任务的下游精确度,以及通过客观要素计量和基于LLM的法官评估推理质量. 前者衡量模型是否产生正确答案;后者审查模型是否出于正确原因产生正确答案。

blocks.en: 4.1 Downstream VQA Accuracy
blocks.zh: 4.1 下游VQA 准确性

blocks.en: We frame the task as binary spatial VQA: each question has a Yes / No ground-truth answer derived from GQA’s scene graphs [ 11 ] . Accuracy is computed as exact-match after lower-casing and stripping articles, consistent with the standard GQA evaluation protocol. We additionally report accuracy conditioned on answer polarity ( Yes-acc and No-acc ) to diagnose positive-answer bias, a known marker of language-prior exploitation in VQA models [ 8 , 1 ] .
blocks.zh: 我们把任务设定为二进制空间 VQA : 每个问题都有一个是 / 没有从 GQA 的场景图中得出的地面真实答案 [11] 。 准确性在下级和剥离文章后作为精确匹配计算,符合标准的GQA评价协议. 我们又报告以回答极性为条件的准确性(Yes-acc和No-ac),以诊断正答偏差,这是已知的VQA模型中语言优先开发的标记 [8, 1].

blocks.en: 4.2 Objective Reasoning Metrics
blocks.zh: 4.2 客观理由计量

blocks.en:
We compare each model’s thinking trace against the ground-truth scene-graph reasoning chain using ROUGE-1 and ROUGE-L [ 19 ] , token-level F1 [ 29 ] (after lower-casing and stop-word removal), entity overlap (fraction of scene-graph object labels present in the predicted chain), and length ratio (predicted-to-reference chain length in tokens, a proxy for verbosity). All metrics are computed on all test examples regardless of answer correctness, and stratified by correctness to test whether higher-quality chains co-occur with correct answers.
These metrics measure surface agreement only: multiple valid traces can realise the same relational path (e.g., boy vs. man for one node), and overlap with a Claude-Haiku-generated reference rewards stylistic similarity, which fine-tuned models inherit. No faithfulness conclusion in this paper rests on them.
blocks.zh:
我们用ROUGE-1和ROUGE-L[19]、符号级F1[29](在删除下级和止句之后)、实体重叠(在预测链中存在的场景-图形对象标签被违反)和长度比(在符号中预想到参考链长,作为动词的代名词)来比较每个模型的思维跟踪。 在所有测试实例中计算出所有衡量标准,而不论答案正确与否,并按正确性进行分级,以测试高品质链是否与正确答案一致。
这些度量标准只测量表面协议:多个有效的痕迹可以实现相同的关系路径(例如,一个节点的boy vs. man),并和克洛德-海库所生成的参照奖相重叠,这种参照奖是精细的模型继承的. 本文中没有任何忠实的结论取决于他们。

blocks.en: 4.3 LLM-as-Judge Reasoning Evaluation
blocks.zh: 4.3 LLM-as-Judge 理性评价

blocks.en:
Objective metrics capture only surface-level agreement with the reference output and are insufficient to assess whether a candidate rationale is semantically grounded in the scene representation or whether it covers all inference steps required to justify the answer. We therefore adopt a rubric-based LLM-as-a-judge protocol, following prior work showing that strong LLM judges can approximate human evaluation when guided by explicit criteria, while remaining sensitive to prompt design and bias [ 46 ] . In particular, our prompt is inspired by rubric-based evaluation frameworks such as G-Eval, which uses structured prompting and chain-of-thought to score outputs under custom criteria [ 21 ] . The judge receives the question, ground-truth answer, scene graph, candidate final answer, and candidate reasoning, and returns three normalized scores in [ 0 , 1 ] [0,1] , computed by Claude Sonnet 4.6 [ 2 ] : answer correctness ( 𝐴𝐶 \mathit{AC} ), reasoning faithfulness ( 𝑅𝐹 \mathit{RF} ), and reasoning completeness ( 𝑅𝐶 \mathit{RC} ).
Because the judge scores against the symbolic scene graph rather than the reference text, it is invariant to the surface variation that penalises overlap metrics. We validate it against human annotators and against a second judge from a different provider (GPT-5.6) in Appendix L .
blocks.zh:
客观的衡量标准只反映与参考产出的地表级一致,不足以评估候选人的理由是否完全基于现场表述,或是否涵盖为证明答案有理而必须采取的所有推断步骤。 因此,我们采纳了一种以名义为基础的LLM-as-a-judge协议,此前的研究表明,强有力的LLM法官在以明确标准为指导时可以大致评价人类,同时对迅速设计和偏见保持敏感[46]。 特别是,G-Eval等基于主题的评价框架激励了我们的迅速性,这些框架利用结构化的迅速性和思维链来根据定制标准对产出进行评分[21]。 法官收到问题、地面真相回答、场景图、候选人最后回答和候选人推理,并返回由克洛德·索内(Claude Sonnet)计算出的三个正常分数[0,1][0,1]:回答正确性(AC\mathit{AC})、推理忠实性(RF\mathit{RF})和推理完整性(RC\mathit{RC})。
由于评委根据象征性的场景图而不是参考文本进行评分,因此对表层变异的处罚是相互重叠的度量. 我们在附录L中以人类注释员和来自不同提供者(GPT-5.6)的第二名法官为对象加以验证。

blocks.en: Separating faithfulness from correctness is important because chain-of-thought explanations may be plausible yet unfaithful to the model’s actual inference process [ 34 ] . Likewise, completeness captures whether the rationale accounts for all key spatial constraints and relations needed to support the final answer. Since scene graphs provide a structured representation of entities and relations, they serve as a natural evidence source for this judgment procedure and as the basis for the ground-truth reasoning chains themselves [ 13 , 33 , 45 ] .
blocks.zh: 将忠诚与正确性区分开来很重要,因为思维的一连串解释对于模型的实际推论过程可能可信而不可信[34]。 同样,完整性也说明理由是否说明了支持最后答案所需的所有关键空间限制和关系。 由于场景图提供了实体和关系的有条理的表述,它们成为这一判决程序的自然证据来源并成为地面-真实推理链本身的基础[13、33、45]。

blocks.en: 7 Limitations
blocks.zh: 7 限制

blocks.en:
SpatialChain has five main limitations.
First, GQA scene graphs were annotated by humans and may contain errors
that propagate into the synthetic reasoning chains.
Second, the answer-consistency filter verifies a chain’s conclusion,
not each intermediate step: the generator (Claude Haiku 4.5) can
hallucinate, so retained chains conclude correctly but are not
guaranteed step-correct; per-step verification against scene-graph
node IDs is the natural next step.
Third, the faithfulness judge (Claude Sonnet 4.6) is a single model
from the same family as the reference generator, and one evaluated
system shares that family. The second-judge and human-validation
results (Appendix L ) bound this risk, but
references generated by a non-Claude model remain untested.
Fourth, the task is binary Yes / No with a 58 % 58\% yes-rate in training, which enables Δ pol \Delta_{\text{pol}} but caps the
accuracy axis and is amplified by SFT; extending beyond binary VQA is
the focus of future versions.
Fifth, scene-graph relations are symbolic rather than metric, so the
benchmark does not capture full geometric understanding (e.g., exact
distances or 3D depth), and the complexity-biased test split is
dominated by projective left / right relations.

blocks.en: 8 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 8 结论

blocks.en:
We introduced SpatialChain , a dataset pairing spatially grounded
GQA questions with scene-graph-consistent reasoning chains,
enabling training and structured evaluation of spatial reasoning
in thinking-enabled VLMs.
Chain quality significantly predicts answer correctness across most
models; the judge evaluation reveals that high accuracy frequently
coexists with shortcut rates above 39% — evidence that answer
scores alone are insufficient to characterize spatial reasoning
ability — and this signal survives a change of judge, a sweep of
the threshold, and comparison with human annotators.
SFT improves in-domain accuracy while exposing a stylistic
trade-off on external benchmarks, motivating replay-augmented
training as a future direction.
Beyond SFT, SpatialChain supports reinforcement learning —
outcome and process rewards can be computed automatically from
the verifiable answer and scene-graph reference — and provides
structured spatial supervision for Vision-Language-Action
models [ 28 , 43 ] , where object-relation
understanding is a prerequisite for manipulation and navigation.
We hope SpatialChain encourages the community to interrogate
the reasoning process behind model predictions, beyond
the final answer.

blocks.en:
Two patterns emerge beyond what the main table captures.
Token precision vs. recall separates models by how they
fail: proprietary models (Claude 4.6, GPT-5.4, InternVL3.5-4B)
show high precision but very low recall, confirming that their
compact outputs contain relevant words but cover only a
small fraction of the reference content.
Open-weight base models (Qwen3-VL-4B/8B) exhibit the reverse —
moderate precision but high recall — consistent with their
verbose, exploratory chains.
Step markers provide a direct proxy for explicit
step-by-step structure: fine-tuned models average 0.26–0.45
per chain (matching the reference format), while open-weight base
models average 2–3 (enumerating more steps than the reference),
and proprietary models score 0.00, indicating the near-total
absence of explicit reasoning structure.
The entity overlap column further confirms that fine-tuned models
( ≈ 0.48 \approx 0.48 ) reference scene-graph objects more faithfully
than any other group, despite generating shorter chains.

blocks.en: L.5 Single-Hop vs. Multi-Hop Questions
blocks.zh: L.5 单霍普与多霍普问题

blocks.en:
We stratified the test set by hop count — the number of spatial
relations chained in the question, inferred from the question text
(385 single-hop, 509 multi-hop, 5 ambiguous cases classified by
hand) — and recomputed accuracy and faithfulness per stratum
(Table 18 ). The effect is small and, for most models,
runs mildly opposite to the intuition that multi-hop is harder:
accuracy averages + 0.019 +0.019 higher on multi-hop and faithfulness + 0.014 +0.014 higher, with the Qwen3 base models showing the clearest
positive shift. The two models most associated with shortcuts,
InternVL3.5-4B/8B, are flat or slightly negative. We read this as
evidence that the dominant difficulty is perceiving the individual
relation rather than composing several.
